evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: This call will just take around ten to fifteen minutes. Will that work? — framing present but no dependable-quote language, and rushed past without real wait for affirmation.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: I'd like to ask first what are your biggest concerns and what are the most important things you want answers to on this call today aside from code? — asked before probing.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Eric raises moving two apartments on the same day; Nicole says 'we can definitely do that' and moves on. Eric raises TV box concern; Nicole answers but doesn't probe deeper into his concern. No genuine 'tell me more' follow-ups on concerns raised.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: None. Nicole acknowledges concerns but never summarizes back what she heard (e.g., 'So what I'm hearing is you want both moves on the same day, and you're concerned about TV packing'). This is absent.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (apartment/house), floor/stories (second floor, ground floor, one-story house), rooms (one bedroom x2), walking distance (50 feet, 20-25 feet, driveway), special considerations (TVs, frames, beds, couch), additional stops (two apartments to one house). All seven covered.
evidence_quotes.packing_services_offered: Not asked. Nicole mentions TV wrapping and boxes but never offers packing services.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Asked: 'for a typical one bedroom apartment we usually expect to see around fifteen to twenty boxes... Do you think you alone will fall within that range?' and for friend.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Gave typical range ('two and a half to three and a half hours for a typical one bedroom') and personalized to this move ('since you're moving from a second floor apartment, and picking up your friend's items from a first floor apartment...Moving to a one story house with thirty minutes drive between location'). Full estimate: $1,144 to $1,352.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Disclosed hourly rate ($208/hr for two movers, one truck), what's included (fuel, insurance, pads, tools, assembly/reassembly), no hidden fees, 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments stated. All present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Never asked 'Does that feel fair?' after the estimate. Moved directly to 'to secure a spot, there's no deposit required.'
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Full: 'if we cannot make it in the time window that we arrange, we immediately start discounting money of your final bill'—clearly states discount terms and immediacy.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Full: 'We provide up to $2,000 per move to repair replace or reimburse for any accidental damages' and included in rate (no mention of deductible/fine print, no add-on language).
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: No. Nicole never asks 'Does that put those to rest?' or similar to confirm the two promises landed.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Throwaway. 'And do you have any questions or anything for me?' — empty, automatic-no phrasing, not genuine version like 'What's still concerning you?'
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Not asked. No version of 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?'
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: With out. 'And would you like our help with your move?' asked, but then Eric says 'are you able to like email this to me' and Nicole immediately agrees and offers email without pushing back, creating an easy exit.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Not mentioned. No language about rate holding or locking in the price.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: Partial. Nicole confirmed: email address (Eric Mendez67@gmail.com), follow-up method (email reply or call 9 AM–5:30 PM). Missing: move date (October 26th was mentioned by customer but not re-confirmed as booked), phone number (assumed from intake but not re-confirmed), arrival window, crew size, both addresses (mentioned earlier but not re-confirmed at close), and no crew notes left about customer concerns.

top_strength: Nicole gathered all critical logistics details efficiently—both apartment locations, floors, item weights, TV concern, box counts, parking distances, and destination property—setting up a highly accurate estimate without wasting time.
coaching_note: Never ask 'Does that feel fair?' after pricing—this is a critical objection-readiness moment—and stop offering email-out when the customer hesitates instead of booking; lean in with urgency and a real close instead.
